# SQLForm - llms.txt

> LLM-readable manifest (https://llmstxt.org). Features-only; no fabricated traffic or KYB claims.

## Name & positioning
- Product name: SQLForm
- One-line value: SQLForm turns natural-language questions into read-oriented SQL drafts with deterministic safety checks (e.g. destructive statements) — decision-support for analysts, not auto-exec.
- Domain: https://sqlfix.lxsaihub.com/
- Language: English (en)

## Domain context (verified primary sources)
- ISO/IEC 9075 SQL overview (Wikipedia summary hub): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SQL
- OWASP Query Parameterization Cheat Sheet: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Query_Parameterization_Cheat_Sheet.html

## FAQ (high-signal Q&A for AI citation)
Q1. Does it execute SQL on my database?
A1. No. It drafts SQL text for you to review. Execution stays in your tools.
Q2. How does it reduce risk?
A2. Rule checks flag destructive patterns (DROP/DELETE without WHERE, etc.) before you run anything.
Q3. Which dialects?
A3. Drafts are generally ANSI-leaning; adjust identifiers for your warehouse dialect.
Q4. Is Demo mode live AI?
A4. Demo is labelled and does not require a live key.
Q5. Who is it for?
A5. Analysts and PMs who want a first-pass SELECT with safety annotations.
Q6. Primary guidance?
A6. Treat SQL as untrusted until reviewed; follow your org's data-access policy.
